title: Development of a performance portable distributed FFT interface on top of the Kokkos ecosystem
problem: Developing distributed FFT implementations that maintain performance portability across diverse HPC hardware architectures (CPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs) while simplifying implementation complexity.
motivation: FFT is a fundamental operation in scientific computing; existing implementations often lack portability or require extensive hardware-specific optimization. Kokkos ecosystem provides abstraction layer but distributed FFT interface was missing.
method: Leveraged Kokkos and kokkos-fft libraries to develop a performance-portable distributed FFT layer with new features including batched-distributed FFT and interfaces to vendor-optimized libraries.
key_novelty: Batched-distributed FFT capability; unified interface to vendor libraries (cuFFT, rocFFT) through Kokkos abstraction; performance portability across GPU and CPU platforms.
contributions: Performance-portable distributed FFT implementation on top of Kokkos
Interfaces to vendor-optimized distributed FFT libraries
Demonstrated efficiency on NVIDIA A100 and AMD MI250X GPUs with CPU fallback

metrics.performance: Efficient performance demonstrated on A100 and MI250X

limitations: Abstract only; unclear specific performance gains; limited details on scalability aspects.
